notes.meaning: Jesus told the people to pay their taxes to the Roman ruler, while also giving their full devotion to God. Using Caesar's coins showed that they lived under his civil rule and benefited from it. But because human beings bear God's image, their whole lives belong to God.

differ.view: Lutherans teach that Jesus reveals two distinct realms: the earthly government that keeps order through reason, and God's spiritual kingdom that rules the heart and conscience.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Early church teachers saw Caesar's image on the coin as a reminder that God's image is stamped on the human soul, meaning believers must offer their whole selves back to God.

notes.meaning: The spies could find nothing in Jesus' words to accuse Him of treason or rebellion before the crowd. His wise answer surprised them so completely that they could say nothing in return. They were left silenced and defeated in public.

The Sadducees were a wealthy ruling party that rejected the supernatural, including angels, spirits, and the resurrection of the dead. They came to Jesus with a question designed to make the hope of rising from the dead look foolish.

Their question was built on an ancient law from the books of Moses. If a married man died without having children, his brother was required to marry the widow so that a child could carry on the dead man's family line and property.
The Sadducees presented a story about seven brothers. The oldest brother married a wife and died without leaving any children to inherit his family name.

Following the law, the second brother married the widow, but he also died childless. The third brother did the same, and eventually all seven brothers married her and died without children. At last, the woman died as well.

The Sadducees thought their riddle proved that the resurrection could not make sense. Because all seven brothers had been married to the same woman, they asked whose wife she would be in the world to come.
Jesus pointed out that they were confusing life on earth with life in heaven. In this present world, people die, so marriage and childbearing are necessary to carry on the human race.
Those who are granted eternal life enter an entirely new way of living. In the age to come, people neither marry nor arrange marriages, because earthly family lines are no longer needed there.
In the resurrection, believers can never die again, which makes them like the angels in immortality. Because they have been raised to endless life, they are openly revealed as God's own children.

Jesus defended the resurrection using the writings of Moses, the scriptures the Sadducees trusted most. At the burning bush, the Lord introduced Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob centuries after those patriarchs had died.
God cannot be the God of people who have ceased to exist. Since God still claims Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as His own, they must still be alive to Him in spirit and waiting for their bodies to rise.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars suggest the phrase saying all are alive to God was an explanatory note added by Luke, since it does not appear in Matthew or Mark.

notes.meaning: Some scribes belonged to the Pharisees, who strongly believed in the resurrection. They were delighted to see Jesus defeat their rivals, the Sadducees, and openly praised His answer.
After Jesus answered the questions about taxes and the resurrection with such wisdom, His critics lost their nerve. Neither group dared to ask Him any more trick questions.

Jesus now went on the offensive and questioned the religious teachers about the Messiah, God's chosen King. Everyone agreed that the Messiah would be a physical descendant of King David, but Jesus pressed them to see that there was more to the story.

Jesus quoted Psalm 110, where King David spoke by God's Spirit about a conversation between God the Father and the Messiah. The Father invited the Messiah to sit at His right hand in the place of highest honor until all His enemies were brought under His control.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars question whether King David actually wrote Psalm 110, suggesting it was written by a later author.

notes.meaning: Jesus asked how the Messiah could simply be David's son if David himself called Him 'Lord.' The only answer is that the Messiah is a human descendant of David according to the flesh, but also the divine Son of God.
Jesus turned to speak to His disciples while the whole crowd was listening. He wanted everyone to hear His warning so that ordinary people would not be led astray by corrupt leaders.

Jesus told His followers to watch out for the scribes, who loved to show off their importance. They walked around in fancy flowing robes and craved public praise in the markets, along with the best seats in the synagogues and at banquets.

Beneath their pious image and long prayers, these teachers cheated helpless widows out of their homes and property. Because they used religion as a disguise for their greed, God will punish them with far greater severity.
